result:
The house remembers what we forget. At dusk, when the sun bleeds amber through the east window, dust motes rise like slow constellations. I watch them drift above the floorboards, each one a fragment of a life lived in haste. The floor creaks a familiar song, the same pitch it held when I was small, when this room was full of shouting and spilled juice and shoes dragged across the threshold. Now it holds only silence.

Outside, a wind chime taps against the porch railing, keeping time with something invisible. I press my palm to the cold glass. A leaf drifts across the driveway. The air smells of damp soil and distant woodsmoke. The neighborhood settles into its evening rhythm: a porch light flickers on, a dog barks twice, a car passes without slowing. Everything moves forward, but this room refuses to. It hoards shadows in the corners, stacks them like unread books, waits for footsteps that will never return.

I used to think time was a straight line, marching from past to future. Now I know it pools. It gathers in abandoned places, settles into the grain of worn wood, lingers in the space between breaths. When I leave tonight, I will lock the door. But the house won’t sleep. It will keep breathing in the dark, holding the quiet like a secret, waiting for dawn to wash the dust into gold again.
